key_insight: SCAPS-1D optimization shows that an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 stack can strongly improve charge separation and yield a predicted 28.44% efficiency for CNGS thin-film solar cells.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical device-design roadmap for tuning absorber, transport layers, interfaces, and operating conditions in earth-abundant thin-film photovoltaics.
method: Simulated an In2S3/CNGS/MoTe2 heterostructure in SCAPS-1D.
Optimized thickness, doping, defect density, recombination, resistance, temperature, and illumination.
Analyzed band alignment, electric fields, carrier distributions, and generation-recombination behavior.
evidence_signal: Under AM1.5G illumination at 300 K, the optimized device is reported to reach 28.44% PCE with 0.984 V VOC, 34.39 mA/cm2 JSC, and 84.04% FF, outperforming the 6.25–21.17% range cited for prior CNGS devices.
watch_item: The results are purely computational, so experimental validation is still needed to confirm interface quality, defect assumptions, and achievable material stability.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
